A.summary:
This change adds a database table, patchset_maintainer_sections, that
records which MAINTAINERS file sections a patchset touches. It mirrors the
existing bug_subsystems table. A bug's recorded sections decide who may read
its transcripts, but a patchset only had mailing list labels taken from
To:/Cc: headers. Anyone can put an address in Cc:, and those labels name
lists rather than people, so they cannot be used for access decisions.

Each row carries a source column, and only rows whose source is
maintainers_section confer authority. The default source is the least
privileged value, caller_supplied, so a writer that omits provenance
grants nobody anything.

The change includes these parts:

- A version 9 schema migration, run in a transaction, with two indexes.
  One of them is partial and covers only the authorizing rows.
- add_patchset_maintainer_sections, a union operation for ingestion. A
  series arrives one part at a time, and each part contributes the sections
  its own files touch.
- replace_patchset_maintainer_sections, which sets the list to exactly the
  given sections and prunes stale rows. It is meant for backfill.
- authorizing_sections_for_patchset, which returns only maintainers_section
  rows.
- patchset_maintainer_sections, which returns every row with its provenance,
  for display only.

Tests cover union across series parts, only maintainers rows conferring
authority, an empty patchset authorizing nobody, pruning and re-attribution
on replace, and no leakage between patchsets.

Nothing reads or writes these rows yet, so there is no user-visible or
agent-visible effect. The one runtime change is that existing databases are
migrated to version 9 on startup.
A.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::add_patchset_maintainer_sections and
  UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL), the upsert does ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET
  source = excluded.source, so when two parts of a series name the same
  section with different provenance the last part to arrive decides the
  stored source. A maintainers_section row downgraded to path_prefix or
  caller_supplied stops being returned by authorizing_sections_for_patchset,
  and the real maintainers silently lose access to raw transcripts. The doc
  comment says add must not narrow the attribution, and the function returns
  Ok with no log. Replace has the same last-duplicate-wins behaviour via the
  BTreeMap collect. The failure is closed and nothing reads the rows yet, so
  it is latent. Fix: in the add path never lower provenance, and leave
  demotion to replace.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections and
  add_patchset_maintainer_sections), the SELECT, per-row DELETEs and per-row
  UPSERTs each run as separate autocommit statements with no transaction. An
  error part way (busy database, I/O error, dropped future) persists a
  half-applied set: a wanted section can be missing, or a row meant to be
  demoted keeps maintainers_section and still confers authority. The bug-side
  equivalent, update_bug_subsystems, is wrapped in a transaction. No
  non-test caller exists yet, so this is latent. Fix: wrap both bodies in a
  transaction.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (create_patchset, merge of duplicate patchsets), the
  merge carries patchsets_subsystems to the surviving patchset but never
  copies patchset_maintainer_sections. DELETE FROM patchsets then fires ON
  DELETE CASCADE (foreign_keys is ON), silently destroying the merged-away
  patchset's sections. The surviving patchset's attribution is narrowed or
  emptied, which contradicts the documented union semantics, and
  authorizing_sections_for_patchset returns a false 'nobody responsible'
  result. It fails closed and nothing writes these rows outside tests yet,
  so it is latent, but the loss is unrecoverable without a backfill. Fix:
  before the delete, INSERT OR IGNORE the rows into the target, giving
  maintainers_section precedence when the same subsystem exists on both
  rows, and add a merge test. This issue was not introduced by edits to the
  merge code; it is an omission of this change.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (test_patchset_sections_union_across_parts), the
  only duplicate re-added has an identical name and source, so the source
  overwrite is a no-op and the test passes whether or not the upsert
  clobbers provenance. No test adds the same name as maintainers_section and
  then as path_prefix in either order, or passes conflicting duplicates to
  replace, or fails part way through replace. The order-dependent downgrade
  in add would go undetected.

- [MEDIUM] In src/migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql (CREATE
  TABLE patchset_maintainer_sections), the DEFAULT 'caller_supplied' and the
  CHECK on source are the migration's central safety claim, but no test
  covers them. Every new test writes through add_ or replace_, which always
  bind source. Changing the default to maintainers_section or dropping the
  CHECK leaves all tests passing. Needed: a test that inserts without the
  column and asserts the authorizing list is empty, and that an invalid
  source errors.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections),
  the prune loop is the only thing that removes authority from a patchset,
  yet the sole replace test always passes a non-empty list containing a
  surviving name. Adding an early return on an empty wanted set, as add has,
  would leave every test passing while stale maintainers_section rows
  survive when nothing matches any more. Whitespace-padded names are also
  not exercised through replace.

- [LOW] In src/migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql and
  src/db.rs (UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL), changes to the source column of
  patchset_maintainer_sections are not audited, while bug_subsystems has
  trg_bug_subsystems_audit_insert and trg_bug_subsystems_audit_source in
  src/migrations/002_bugs.sql, which record additions and reattribution
  because source decides who can reach the record. A row can move between
  maintainers_section and path_prefix or caller_supplied with nothing
  recorded, so the commit message's claim of mirroring bug_subsystems omits
  the audit behaviour. The add path is also not monotonic in authority: a
  weaker source overwrites a stronger one, and a stronger one silently
  grants, both unrecorded. Nothing reads the rows yet, so this is capped at
  Low. Fix before the transcript rules consume the table, with an audit
  mechanism or an upsert that never lowers source.

findings.problem: patchset section add overwrites source, so arrival order decides authority
findings.explanation: Consequence: when two parts of a series name the same section with different provenance, the stored source is whichever part arrived last. A maintainers_section row downgraded to path_prefix or caller_supplied stops being returned by authorizing_sections_for_patchset, and the real maintainers silently lose access to the raw transcripts. add_patchset_maintainer_sections returns Ok(()) with no log, and its doc comment says a later part must not narrow the attribution. Reachability: UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL ends with ON CONFLICT(patchset_id, subsystem) DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source, and add uses that statement for every entry. Replace has the same last-duplicate-wins behaviour through the BTreeMap collect. The failure direction is closed, not an over-grant, and nothing reads the rows yet, so it is latent. It is Medium rather than Low because it is a wrong result in the table that decides who may read transcripts. Fix: in the add path never lower provenance, for example by only overwriting when excluded.source is maintainers_section, and leave demotion to replace.

locations.code_snippet: ON CONFLICT(patchset_id, subsystem) DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source
locations.why_this_location_matters: Conflict handling replaces provenance instead of keeping the strongest one.
The function documented as add-only can change the authority of an existing row.

findings.problem: patchset section replace/add run as autocommit statements, no transaction
findings.explanation: Consequence: replace_patchset_maintainer_sections does a SELECT, then per-row DELETEs, then per-row UPSERTs, each as its own autocommit on self.conn. An error partway (busy database, I/O error, a future dropped at an await) persists a half-applied set. If the deletes land and an upsert fails, a wanted section is missing. If a name stays in wanted with a changed source, such as maintainers_section demoted to path_prefix, the old row survives and still confers authority that the replace meant to revoke. The doc comment promises that a section which no longer matches stops conferring authority, and the code cannot guarantee that. add_patchset_maintainer_sections is likewise a loop of independent upserts, so an error leaves part of a part's sections written. The diff shows that the bug-side equivalent is wrapped in a transaction (update_bug_subsystems opens self.conn.transaction()), and the patchset functions are pub with no wrapper. Reachability: there are no non-test callers yet, so this is latent. The concurrent-ingestion case, where a backfill replace deletes a section that an add wrote after the backfill computed its union, depends on how the future callers are scheduled and cannot be confirmed from this diff. Fix: wrap the bodies in a transaction.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Delete and upsert phases are separate autocommit statements, so replacement is not all-or-nothing.

findings.problem: patchset merge drops merged patchset maintainer sections
findings.explanation: Consequence: when ingestion merges duplicate patchset rows, every patchset_maintainer_sections row of the merged-away patchset is silently deleted by ON DELETE CASCADE, so the surviving patchset's attribution is narrowed or emptied. The new table is documented as a union that grows as a series lands, and the merge breaks that. Reachability: the merge runs inside create_patchset (src/db.rs:5078) whenever more than one candidate matches (matches.len() > 1, line ~5488), which is the normal path for series parts that arrive out of order or as resends. The whole merge body (5440-5640) was read. It re-points bugs, reviews, patches and baselines, and it copies patchsets_subsystems with INSERT OR IGNORE before deleting. It never touches patchset_maintainer_sections. A grep for the table name finds only the new accessors, the migration and the new tests, and none of them is in the merge. PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON is set at line 1383, with a comment saying cascades are otherwise inert, so the cascade fires at DELETE FROM patchsets WHERE id = ? (line 5608). The existing test test_merge_patchsets_with_dependencies shows the path is exercised. Direction of failure: authorizing_sections_for_patchset returns an empty list, which the doc comment says the transcript rules treat as closed, so maintainers lose access rather than gaining it. The record is lost silently, which is a false 'nobody responsible' result. Calibration: Medium, not higher, because it fails closed and nothing reads or writes these rows outside tests yet (the commit says so), so it is latent today. It becomes live as soon as an ingestion caller starts calling add_patchset_maintainer_sections, and the loss is not recoverable except by a backfill. The analogous patchsets_subsystems handling in the same block shows the omission is an oversight. No test covers merge plus sections, so nothing would fail. Fix: add INSERT OR IGNORE INTO patchset_maintainer_sections (patchset_id, subsystem, source) SELECT target, subsystem, source FROM patchset_maintainer_sections WHERE patchset_id = merge_from, before the delete. Where both rows share a subsystem but differ in source, take the more privileged one, or the stricter one deliberately, instead of letting INSERT OR IGNORE pick by insertion order. Add a merge test.

findings.problem: patchset_maintainer_sections source changes are not audited
findings.explanation: Consequence: any change to which rows grant read authority over a patchset's raw review transcripts leaves no record, while the same change on a bug is recorded. Reachability: add_patchset_maintainer_sections and replace_patchset_maintainer_sections both go through UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL, whose ON CONFLICT clause does 'SET source = excluded.source'. A row can therefore move between 'maintainers_section' (authority) and 'path_prefix' or 'caller_supplied' (no authority) with nothing written anywhere. For example, a later part of a series contributes the same name with a different source, or a backfill re-runs the replace. The new tests even use the name 'net' with both sources. The authorizing index and authorizing_sections_for_patchset read exactly this column. Verified: src/migrations/002_bugs.sql defines trg_bug_subsystems_audit_insert (line 278) and trg_bug_subsystems_audit_source (line 300). The insert trigger writes an 'audit' row to bug_enrichments with action 'subsystem_added'. The source trigger fires on 'AFTER UPDATE OF source ... WHEN old.source <> new.source' and writes action 'subsystem_reattributed' with old and new values. Its own comment says reattribution 'decides whether a maintainer can reach the bug at all, so the change is audited'. That reasoning applies unchanged to patchset transcripts. Migration 009 contains no trigger, so the commit message's 'mirroring bug_subsystems down to the source column' is true for the columns but leaves out the audit behaviour. The dismissal argument that bug_enrichments has no patchset counterpart explains why a trigger can't be copied verbatim. It doesn't show an audit is unneeded, and I did not look for another patchset event store, so where an audit would live is a design decision for the author. Related defect on the same path: the union in add_patchset_maintainer_sections is not monotonic in authority. Its comment says it adds without removing, but a later part supplying an existing name with a weaker source overwrites 'maintainers_section' and silently revokes authority. A stronger source silently grants it, and both are unrecorded. Severity is capped at Low because nothing reads these rows yet ('Nothing reads these rows yet'). It should be fixed, with an audit trigger or an upsert that never lowers source, before the transcript rules start consuming the table.

AFTER UPDATE OF source ON bug_subsystems
FOR EACH ROW
WHEN old.source <> new.source

B.summary:
This commit adds a new database table, patchset_maintainer_sections, that
records which MAINTAINERS sections a patchset touches, along with where
each name came from (a MAINTAINERS match, a directory prefix, or a
caller-supplied string). It mirrors the existing bug_subsystems table so
that one SubsystemSource type serves both.

Only rows sourced from a MAINTAINERS match are meant to confer authority
over who may read a patchset's raw review transcripts. The existing
patchsets_subsystems table holds mailing list labels taken from To:/Cc:
headers, which anyone can influence, so it cannot be used for that decision.

Migration 009 creates the table with a CHECK constraint on the source
column, a least-privileged default of caller_supplied, a cascade delete
tied to patchsets, and two indexes. In src/db.rs it adds four operations:
an add (a union, for ingestion as each part of a series arrives), a
replace (an exact set with pruning, for backfill), a lookup returning only
the authorizing sections, and a display lookup returning every section
with its provenance. Unit tests cover union across parts, authority
limited to MAINTAINERS-sourced rows, empty input, pruning and
reattribution on replace, and isolation between patchsets.

Nothing reads or writes these rows yet, so there is no user-visible
effect.
B.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL,
  add_patchset_maintainer_sections, replace_patchset_maintainer_sections),
  the conflict clause ON CONFLICT(patchset_id, subsystem) DO UPDATE SET
  source = excluded.source lets a weaker source overwrite
  maintainers_section. The conflict key excludes source, so a later part
  supplying the same name as path_prefix or caller_supplied downgrades the
  row, and authorizing_sections_for_patchset silently stops returning it.
  The reverse order upgrades it, so authority depends on part arrival order
  and contradicts the documented union. In replace, the BTreeMap collect
  keeps whichever duplicate name comes last. The tests only repeat
  identical (name, source) pairs, so the overwrite is untested. Use a
  non-downgrading conflict clause, prefer MaintainersSection when
  deduplicating, and add a test for differing sources.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections),
  the deletes and upserts run as separate autocommit statements with no
  transaction. An error or future cancellation between the delete and
  upsert loops leaves the patchset pruned but not repopulated, so
  maintainers silently lose access. A concurrent
  add_patchset_maintainer_sections between the initial SELECT and the
  DELETEs can also have its new row pruned from the stale snapshot. The
  bug-side counterpart is atomic only because update_bug_subsystems wraps
  it in a transaction, and the libsql comment copied into the new function
  describes a transaction that does not exist. The add function is also a
  per-row autocommit loop, though it is additive and idempotent so a retry
  heals it. Run the delete and upsert phase in one transaction.

findings.problem: patchset section upsert lets a weaker source overwrite maintainers_section
findings.explanation: Reasoning: contained data-integrity defect on one patchset's authorization rows. It fails closed, it is silent, and nothing reads these rows yet. UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL ends in ON CONFLICT(patchset_id, subsystem) DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source, and the conflict key excludes source, so a path-prefix row and a MAINTAINERS title with the same text are one row. add_patchset_maintainer_sections is documented as a union that never narrows, but it runs this upsert for every entry. If part 1 stores (X, maintainers_section) and a later part supplies (X, path_prefix) or caller_supplied, the row is downgraded and authorizing_sections_for_patchset (source = 'maintainers_section') silently stops returning X. The reverse order upgrades the row, so the authority depends on arrival order. The same collapse happens inside one call to replace_patchset_maintainer_sections, because the BTreeMap collect keeps whichever duplicate name comes last. The upgrade direction is also an authorization hazard for the future ingestion caller, because AttributedSubsystem::from_maintainers is the only barrier. The tests (test_patchset_sections_union_across_parts) only repeat identical (name, source) pairs, so the overwrite path has no coverage. A fix is a non-downgrading conflict clause, for example SET source = CASE WHEN excluded.source = 'maintainers_section' THEN excluded.source ELSE source END, and preferring MaintainersSection when deduplicating in replace, plus a test for a name arriving with different sources across parts.

findings.explanation: Reasoning: contained atomicity defect on one patchset's authorization rows. It fails closed, and nothing calls the function yet. replace_patchset_maintainer_sections (pub) drains a SELECT, then runs one autocommit DELETE per stale row, then one autocommit upsert per wanted row on self.conn, with no transaction. An error (SQLITE_BUSY, I/O) via ? or cancellation of the future at an .await between the delete and upsert loops leaves the patchset pruned but not repopulated. Maintainers silently lose transcript access until a backfill is rerun, and the doc contract that the set is exactly the list is broken. A concurrent add_patchset_maintainer_sections between the SELECT and the DELETEs can have its freshly added row pruned from the stale snapshot, which loses part of the series union. The bug-side mirror is only atomic because its caller update_bug_subsystems wraps replace_bug_subsystems in a transaction. The libsql comment copied into the new function describes a transaction that does not exist here. add_patchset_maintainer_sections is likewise a per-row autocommit loop, so a mid-loop failure persists only part of one part's contribution. That is additive and idempotent, so a retry heals it. The fix is to run the delete and upsert phase inside one transaction using whatever mechanism update_bug_subsystems uses at this revision.

findings.problem: add_patchset_maintainer_sections lets a later part downgrade source
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the failure is fail-closed (authority is lost, never gained), it affects one patchset at a time, and no writer exists yet, so the trigger is speculative. It could not be confirmed that any planned ingestion caller emits the same section name with two different sources. Severity is therefore Low, not Medium. The original H1 'no callers yet' framing is dismissed separately as staged landing; this finding is the real defect underneath it. add_patchset_maintainer_sections is documented as a union that grows as each part of a series lands, but it writes through UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL, whose conflict clause is 'ON CONFLICT(patchset_id, subsystem) DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source'. If one part contributes a name as maintainers_section and a later part contributes the same name as path_prefix or caller_supplied, the stored row is overwritten with the less privileged source. authorizing_sections_for_patchset filters on source = 'maintainers_section', so the section silently stops conferring authority. The reverse order upgrades it. The final authority therefore depends on part arrival order, which contradicts the doc comment's claim that a later part cannot narrow the attribution. The code is copied from UPSERT_BUG_SUBSYSTEM_SQL, which is correct for the replace semantics on the bug side. For the add operation a union needs a precedence rule, for example never overwriting maintainers_section. The new tests cover only distinct names across parts and never the same name with differing sources. Nothing at HEAD calls the add function outside tests (git_grep over src/), so the defect is latent, but it is introduced by this patch's API shape.

findings.problem: patchset merge drops patchset_maintainer_sections via ON DELETE CASCADE
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the loss is contained to individual merged series, fails closed (maintainers lose transcript access, nobody gains it), and is recoverable by the backfill that recomputes the union from stored diffs. The consequence is therefore a wrong authorization outcome on single patchsets, not data destruction across the database or a privilege widening. It is Medium rather than Low because the attribution is silently lost on a normal ingestion path. Proof: Database::create_patchset in src/db.rs, in the merge loop (around lines 5548-5611 at the target commit), re-points bugs.discovered_in_patchset_id and reviews.patchset_id to target_id. It copies patchsets_subsystems with INSERT OR IGNORE and then deletes the old rows. It carries the baseline over, and finally runs DELETE FROM patchsets WHERE id = ? for merge_from_id. Nothing in that block copies or even mentions patchset_maintainer_sections. A grep for patchset_maintainer_sections across src/ finds it only in the new db.rs helpers and tests (20 matches in db.rs) and in migration 009 (5 matches), so no merge-side handling exists. Migration 009 declares FOREIGN KEY(patchset_id) REFERENCES patchsets(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, and Database::new executes PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON on the connection, so the cascade is live. Every section row attached to merge_from_id is therefore deleted when the merged-away row is deleted. Trigger: a series arrives out of order, so parts are first ingested as separate patchset rows. A later message (for example a cover letter or earlier part) causes create_patchset to merge them. Each part had contributed sections through add_patchset_maintainer_sections (the documented ingestion path), and the merged-away part's sections vanish while target_id keeps only its own. The add helper's doc comment says the attribution is a union across parts so that a narrowing never strips maintainers. The merge path silently performs that narrowing. Consequence: authorizing_sections_for_patchset returns a smaller set, or an empty one, which the transcript rules treat as closed, so maintainers of the lost sections cannot read the transcripts. The patch introduces the table and its cascade without updating the existing merge path, so preexisting is false. Caveat: at this commit nothing writes the rows yet (the commit says 'Nothing reads these rows yet'), so impact materializes once ingestion is wired up. I did not have the Series End Commit identifier, so I could not confirm whether a later patch adds merge handling. The fix is to add an INSERT OR IGNORE INTO patchset_maintainer_sections ... SELECT ?, subsystem, source FROM patchset_maintainer_sections WHERE patchset_id = ? statement (taking care that a maintainers_section source is not downgraded by OR IGNORE on conflict) before the DELETE.

findings.explanation: Reasoning: this is a test-coverage gap, not a demonstrated runtime defect. The implementation looks correct on read (the DELETE and UPSERT are both scoped by patchset_id, and the filter drops empty names), so impact is limited to an unguarded regression in the code that revokes authority. The first passes a non-empty list with one maintainers section and one path prefix. The second passes a single section. No test calls replace with an empty slice, so nothing asserts that an empty replace revokes all authority. The isolation test test_patchset_sections_do_not_leak_between_patchsets only uses add_patchset_maintainer_sections, so no test shows that replacing one patchset leaves another patchset's rows intact. The new behavior is therefore under-tested exactly where it confers or revokes authority.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: 1) Upgrade path: migrate() applies migration 9 as `if current_version < 9 { ... tx.execute_batch(include_str!("migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql")) ... PRAGMA user_version = 9; tx.commit() }`. The same branch runs for a fresh database (version 0, falling through every step) and for a v8 database (version 8). The SQL consists only of CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS statements, with no ALTER, no DML, and no reads or writes of existing tables. A populated v8 database therefore has nothing to preserve or transform, and the statements are idempotent. The setup_db()-based tests (which call db.migrate()) execute the identical statements. The existing upgrade tests (test_migration_repairs_borrowed_series_names, test_migration_folds_shadow_cover_rows, test_migration_retires_folded_bugs_left_in_the_pipeline) cover migrations 4, 6 and 7, which rewrite or delete existing rows. That is the case where an upgrade test earns its keep, and migration 9 is not that case. The version bump and the DDL share one transaction, so a partial failure cannot leave a half-applied v9. 2) Cascade: the table declares `FOREIGN KEY(patchset_id) REFERENCES patchsets(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, mirroring bug_subsystems. Database::new enables foreign keys per connection (the comment at src/db.rs:1380 says 'Without this every ON DELETE CASCADE in the schema is inert'), so the cascade is a declarative schema property rather than new Rust logic. 3) What remains is a possible gap in test breadth, not a defect with a failure mechanism. Nothing reads these rows yet according to the commit message, so no behavior can currently misfire. The migration is trivially additive, so the gap is not worth reporting.
